terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation: in this sense with dē + ablative of the matter
evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 119: dē morte alicujus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The classical word for an official inquiry: quaerere dē a death, a theft, a charge. The inquiry itself is quaestiō (quaestiōnem habēre dē, see trial). Its everyday senses are to look for and to ask (see look-for).
Properly to track, as a hound follows a scent (Cic. N.D. 2.158); then to trace or find out facts. Traupman gives it, and investīgātor, for investigate and investigator. See also research.
To search into a matter; in the courts, of a prosecutor gathering evidence against someone (in aliquem).

terms.gloss: track down, trace (as a hound tracks)
evidence: Cic. Fin. 2.40: ad indāgandum canem (Lewis & Short s.v. ad)
Lewis & Short: “to search carefully, examine thoroughly, explore”
